page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.r7.6xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1843.79 and a multi-core score of 23250.96. Memory bandwidth tests indicate a read-only small block cached speed of 1263.88 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds reached 129.12 GB/sec and 62.93 GB/sec respectively. In application-specific benchmarks, the server demonstrated a PassMark database operations score of 11538.47 and processed 23.5 million Redis SET operations per second.

For specialized workloads, the processor's instruction set includes AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic accelerations like AES and SHA-NI. These instructions support tasks such as LLM inference, where the instance achieved a strong text generation speed of 283.7 tokens/sec using a small 135M model, alongside an average speed of 14.18 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Given its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.r7.6xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound enterprise applications, database hosting, and caching layers that require substantial RAM without the overhead of local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.
